description.narrative:
The Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat) published the results of the Child Labour Force Survey in March 2020. There is a continuous decreasing trend in number of children in economic activity in Turkey. Accordingly, the number of children in the age group of 5-17 engaged in economic activity decreased from 900 thousand in 2021 to 720 thousand in 2020.
The Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MoLSS) is coordinating the implementation of the National Programme on the Elimination of Child Labour (2017-2023) and its Action Plan. Specifically, in 2020 and 2021 :
-New inter-ministerial "Combatting Child Labour Units” were established in all 81 provinces in 2020, involving officials from Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Social Services, Ministry of Education and Social Security Institution with more than 500 dedicated staff. Their main duties are, identification and monitoring of child labour; withdrawal of working children from the workforce; ensuring that children and their families have access to the public services they need.
-A "Seasonal Agricultural Worker Information System (E-METÝP System)” was developed for Improving the Working and Living Conditions of Seasonal Migrant Agricultural Workers. It is a newly developed system to gather all the data relating to the status of seasonal agricultural worker families and their children in one single repository, to monitor the access of seasonal agricultural workers to services, to track the school attendance and performance of the children withdrawn from labour. With support from the EU, Ferrero and CAOBISCO (Association of Chocolate, Biscuit and Confectionary Industries) the ILO provided technical assistance to the Government through various programmes and projects in the areas of capacity building, promoting partnerships, improving legislation and enforcement, building and using the knowledge base on child labour, awareness-raising, and social dialogue. Specifically, through the projects, the ILO contributed to the improvement of the E-METIP system of the government by incorporation of new modules into the existing database on seasonal agricultural workers and their children. These new modules would provide necessary information for better monitoring and tracking of children in a systematic manner, and enable data sharing and integrated action among relevant Ministries. Based on the intervention methodology developed by ILO Turkey in collaboration with national partners; in 2020 and 2021; 3335 Children (1546 M +1789 F) withdrawn/prevented from work in seasonal agriculture and referred to education (formal/non-formal) or early childcare services in 14 recipient target provinces. As part of the 2021 International Year for the Elimination of Child Labour and 12 June World Day Against Child Labour a series of awareness-raising events were organised in cooperation with the constituents.
